newsitem.title: UK: Littlewoods pressured to explain snubbed bid - paper.
newsitem.headline: Littlewoods pressured to explain snubbed bid - paper.

text.p: Pressure is mounting on James Ross, the chairman of Littlewoods the privately owned retail-to-football pools group, to explain why he rejected a rival 540 million stg bid for the group's entire chain of high street stores, said an article in the Independent newspaper.
The rival bid was tabled on May 29 by venture capital firm CVC Capital Partners and backed by Nomura, said the article.

Under the deal Littlewoods would have also been granted board representation and an equity stake in the new business. CVC offered to pay 550 million stg for the chain of 135 shops of which 520 million stg was in cash with a further 30 million stg in the form of loan notes, said the paper.

On Thursday Littlewoods agreed to an offer from British retailer Marks and Spencer Plc to buy 19 stores from Littlewoods for 192.5 million stg, giving it an extra 600,000 square feet of selling space in key town and city centres.

The decision is expected to come under scrutiny when the Moores family, who control Littlewoods, hold one of their regular meetings on Tuesday when the group also publishes its annual results, said the paper.
